name: Museo Experimental El Eco
key_features: Narrowing corridor, coloured walls and a courtyard sculpture, built as 'emotional architecture'.

name: Teresa Carreño Cultural Complex
by: Tomás Lugo Marcano, Jesús Sandoval, Dietrich Kunckel
key_features: Exposed concrete volumes with deep terraces and a monumental fly tower over open plazas.

name: Gabriel García Márquez Cultural Center
key_features: Brick terraces, ramps and a circular courtyard, open as a public route through the block.

name: SOMISA Building
key_features: Welded steel frame with an aluminium and glass curtain wall on a narrow corner site.

name: Praça das Artes
key_features: Pigmented concrete volumes threaded between old buildings, opening a passage through the block.

name: Juscelino Kubitschek Bridge
key_features: Three asymmetric steel arches crossing the deck diagonally like a skipping stone.

name: Schocken Library
key_features: Jerusalem-stone block with a long ribbon of windows: Mendelsohn's modernism adapted to local stone.

name: Wohl Centre
key_features: A tilted, metal-clad volume shaped like an open book cantilevers over a solid base.

name: Santo André Civic Centre
key_features: City hall, council chamber and theatre stand apart on a large plaza with gardens by Burle Marx.

name: KAFD Metro Station
key_features: Undulating sine-wave forms wrap stacked platform levels in a perforated screen that shades the interior.

name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
key_features: Textured concrete cube on a landscaped plinth, with a glass escalator tube projecting from the facade.

name: National Museum – Architecture
key_features: Square glass-walled pavilion under a heavy concrete roof, set beside a neoclassical bank building.

name: National Crafts Museum
key_features: Village-like cluster of low pavilions along a meandering open-air street of courtyards.

name: Open Hand Monument
key_features: Sheet-metal hand that turns in the wind above a sunken amphitheatre, the Trench of Consideration.

name: Shaheed Minar, Dhaka
key_features: Slender white frames on a stepped platform, the central one bowed like a mother over her children.

name: Jim Thompson House
key_features: Old teak houses moved and joined on stilts beside a canal, in a dense tropical garden.

name: Independence Monument (Cambodia)
key_features: Lotus-shaped tower in the form of an Angkorian temple spire, layered with naga heads.

name: Kempegowda International Airport Terminal 2
key_features: A terminal set in gardens, with bamboo-clad ceilings and hanging plants through the halls.

name: Kigali Convention Centre
key_features: Spiral-patterned dome inspired by the roof of the royal palace at Nyanza, lit in colour at night.

name: King Fahd National Library
key_features: Old library wrapped in a cube of white tensile fabric diamonds held by steel cables.

name: Grand National Assembly of Turkey
key_features: Stone-clad parliament with a tall colonnaded front set on a monumental axis.

name: Faculty of Architecture, University of Porto
key_features: Studio pavilions lined along a terrace above the Douro, framing a triangular courtyard.

name: Kaze-no-Oka Crematorium
key_features: A brick octagon, Cor-ten hall and concrete wing sit in a landscaped park, sequenced by controlled light.

name: Leicester University Engineering Building
key_features: Red brick and tile towers with cantilevered lecture halls, beside workshops under diagonal glazed roofs.

name: Lycée Schorge
key_features: Laterite stone classrooms ring a courtyard, with wind towers and a screen of eucalyptus poles.

name: METU Faculty of Architecture
key_features: Board-marked concrete studios around courts and a skylit hall, on the campus pedestrian spine.

name: Magney House
key_features: Long single-room-deep pavilion under a folded corrugated-steel roof, with louvres along the north side.

name: Mapungubwe Interpretation Centre
key_features: Thin timbrel vaults of local stabilised-earth tiles rise from the landscape like rock outcrops.

name: Multihalle Mannheim
key_features: Double-curved timber lath gridshell, laid flat then pushed up into shape, covering a free-form hall.

name: Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech
key_features: Terracotta brick walls laid in woven patterns wrap galleries around a circular courtyard.

name: Notre-Dame du Raincy
key_features: A reinforced-concrete church on slender columns, its walls made of precast screens of coloured glass.

name: Palace of Justice (Punjab and Haryana High Court)
key_features: A huge concrete parasol roof shades the courts, with colossal coloured pylons framing the entrance.

name: Rokko Housing
key_features: Concrete units on a regular grid step down a steep slope, each terrace on the roof of the unit below.

name: San Cataldo Cemetery
key_features: A roofless cubic ossuary and a conical tower on an axis framed by long ranges of burial niches.

name: Social Security Complex, Zeyrek
key_features: Small linked blocks with projecting upper floors and a concrete frame fit the old street scale.

name: Space Group Building
key_features: A dark brick office of split levels, low ceilings and small linked rooms, wrapped in ivy beside a hanok.

name: St. Louis Lambert International Airport Terminal 1
key_features: Repeated thin-shell concrete groin vaults over a column-free hall, with glazed walls between them.

name: Takasugi-an
key_features: Tiny tea house perched high on two chestnut tree trunks, reached by a ladder.

name: Vidhan Bhavan
key_features: A circular wall encloses a mandala-like grid of courts, gardens and chambers for the state assembly.

name: Woodland Cemetery
key_features: Pine forest landscape where a long path passes a granite cross toward the crematorium portico.

name: Final Wooden House
key_features: Hut made entirely of stacked solid cedar beams that act as floor, seat and wall at once.

name: Flower Kiosk, Malmö Eastern Cemetery
key_features: Tiny concrete shed with a tilted roof and frameless glazing clipped to the outside of the walls.

name: Grand Parc Bordeaux Transformation
by: Lacaton & Vassal, Frédéric Druot, Christophe Hutin
key_features: Social housing blocks extended with prefabricated winter gardens and balconies added across the facades.

name: Hu Huishan Memorial
key_features: Tent-shaped hut of bricks made from earthquake rubble, lined in pink and filled with a girl's belongings.

name: Institute of Foreign Languages
key_features: Brise-soleil walls, raised blocks and shaded walkways designed for cross-ventilation in the tropics.

name: Jetwing Lighthouse
key_features: Hotel on a rocky headland; its spiral stair winds round Laki Senanayake's bronze battle sculpture.

name: La Collina Omihachiman
key_features: Sweets shop and café buried under a sweeping roof planted with grass.

name: La Lira Theatre Public Space
key_features: Open Corten steel canopy framing a public square on the site of a demolished theatre by the river.

name: La Tallera
key_features: Concrete lattice walls and a new plaza, with Siqueiros's murals turned to face the street.

name: Menara Tabung Haji
key_features: Round tower held by five external columns, its form drawn from a drum and the five pillars of Islam.

name: Menara UMNO
key_features: Slim tower with wing walls that catch the wind and steer it into the floors for natural cooling.

name: Mestizo Restaurant
key_features: Long black concrete roof slab resting on huge granite boulders at the edge of a park.

name: Monterrey Housing
key_features: Half-built row houses stacked as duplexes, leaving empty bays for families to fill in over time.

name: Norwegian Wild Reindeer Pavilion
key_features: Glass box with a milled pine wall shaped like eroded rock, facing across the Dovrefjell mountains.

name: Nur Alem
key_features: A glass sphere with integrated photovoltaics and wind turbines, built as the Expo 2017 national pavilion.

name: Oberrealta Chapel
key_features: Tiny concrete chapel shaped like a child's drawing of a house, alone on an alpine meadow.

name: Oita Prefectural Library (Art Plaza)
key_features: Hollow precast concrete beams project from the facade as tubes, expressing structure and services.

name: Potato Head Beach Club
key_features: Curved wall clad in hundreds of reclaimed wooden window shutters, wrapping a lawn and pool.

name: Ramses Wissa Wassef Art Centre
key_features: Mud-brick domed and vaulted workshops and houses for weavers, built with Nubian techniques.

name: San Francisco Federal Building
key_features: Narrow slab with a perforated steel sunscreen, natural ventilation and skip-stop lifts.

name: San Miguel Corporation Building
key_features: Office block wrapped in stepped planted terraces and deep sunshades, a tropical take on the tower.

name: Skopje Telecommunications Centre
key_features: Rhythmic concrete towers with flared crowns above a long podium of postal and service halls.

name: Soulages Museum
key_features: Row of Corten steel boxes cantilevered from a slope, with gallery light through glazed ends.

name: Surgical Clinic and Health Centre
key_features: Compressed earth brick wards under a floating double roof, with coloured windows and shaded courts.

name: Swiss National Park Visitor Centre
key_features: Two interlocking white concrete cubes with identical windows and a looping stair between them.

name: The Hive, Nanyang Technological University
key_features: Cluster of rounded towers of tutorial rooms around a central atrium, in textured concrete.

name: The Museum Hotel Antakya
key_features: Hotel raised on a steel deck above excavated Roman mosaics, with rooms as prefabricated modules.

name: Tossols-Basil Athletics Track
key_features: Running track threaded through an oak wood, with trees left standing inside the field.

name: Tulou Collective Housing
key_features: A ring of low-cost rental units around a court reinterprets the Hakka earthen roundhouse.

name: Umbrella House (Kasa no Ie)
key_features: Small square house under a timber umbrella roof of rafters radiating from the centre.

name: Villa Verde Housing
key_features: Timber-framed gabled half-houses, one half built and the other left under the roof for owners to finish.

name: wNw Bar
key_features: Bamboo arches form a dome with a top opening; air cooled over the surrounding lake flows through.

name: Kumano Kodo Nakahechi Museum of Art
key_features: A thin-roofed single-storey box wrapped in layers of clear and milky glass.

name: The Index
key_features: Slim slab tower with service cores at its ends shielding low sun, and shaded long facades.

name: Hoenheim-Nord Tram Terminus
key_features: Tilted concrete canopy and car park whose white lines and light strips follow the movement of cars and trams.

name: IBM Research Centre, La Gaude
key_features: Y-shaped wings raised on sculpted concrete piers, with deep precast window frames.

name: Orange Cube
key_features: Orange perforated metal cube by the Saône, hollowed by a huge conical void for light and views.

name: Rue des Suisses Housing
key_features: Street fronts behind folding metal shutters; in the garden, low blocks wrapped in rolling wooden blinds.

name: LUMA Arles Tower
key_features: A 56 m tower of stacked stainless-steel boxes twisting up from a glass drum that echoes the Roman arena.

name: Musée Jean Cocteau, Séverin Wunderman Collection
key_features: A low white box on the seafront, its glass walls behind a fringe of irregular dark concrete fins.

name: Villa dall'Ava
key_features: Two boxes on thin, randomly tilted columns, with a rooftop pool aimed at the Eiffel Tower.

name: Pavillon Noir
key_features: A dance centre in a glass box held by a black concrete exoskeleton of slanting struts.

name: Le Volcan
key_features: A white truncated cone and a smaller one rise from a sunken public square.

name: Upper Lawn Pavilion
key_features: Weekend house: a timber and glass box set on and inside the old stone walls of a farm cottage.

name: Hopkins House
key_features: Two-storey steel-frame and glass box, entered by a bridge from the street at upper level; open plan inside.

name: Haus Gugalun
key_features: Old log farmhouse extended into the slope with new timber rooms under one continuous gable roof.

name: Mausoleo delle Fosse Ardeatine
by: Mario Fiorentino, Giuseppe Perugini, Nello Aprile, Cino Calcaprina, Aldo Cardelli
key_features: A single huge concrete slab hovers low over the rows of tombs, lit by a thin band of light at its edge.

name: Ponte Musmeci (Viadotto dell'Industria)
key_features: A continuous thin concrete membrane, form-found from soap-film models, carries the deck over four spans.

name: Genova San Giorgio Bridge
key_features: A steel deck shaped like a ship's hull on elliptical concrete piers, replacing the collapsed Morandi bridge.

name: Fondazione Giangiacomo Feltrinelli
key_features: A long, thin glass-and-concrete gabled building whose steep roof repeats the rhythm of its frame.

name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
key_features: Brick-faced volumes and deep slots of light lead visitors on a slow route through the collection.

name: Weekend House, Anavyssos
key_features: Thick local-stone piers carry a flat concrete slab, making a shaded portico that wraps two sides of a small house.

name: Silver Hut
key_features: Ito's own house: a courtyard under a field of thin steel-frame vaults, light enough to feel like a tent.

name: SunnyHills at Minami-Aoyama
key_features: A cake shop wrapped in a cloud of interlocking timber strips (jigoku-gumi joinery) that filters the light.

name: Stone Museum (Stone Plaza)
key_features: Old rice stores linked by new walls of thin local Ashino stone louvres and stone screens with gaps for light.

name: Gifu Kitagata Apartment
key_features: A one-room-thick housing slab whose facade grid is punched with double-height open terraces.

name: Garden & House
key_features: A 4 m wide stack of bare concrete slabs with no outside walls: plants, clear railings and curtains make the facade.

name: Roof House
key_features: The gently sloping roof is the living room: a deck for meals, cooking and showers, reached by ladders.

name: Seoul Olympic Stadium
key_features: Its rim rises and dips like the curve of a Joseon white porcelain vase, over a two-tier bowl.

name: Seoul City Hall
key_features: Double-skin facade whose overhang recalls the eaves of traditional Korean houses; a green wall inside.
